case.headline: A report overlaps this 150.7 ppb episode, but the fit is partial.

reasoning.claim: The monitor recorded 150.7 ppb at its peak on Feb 25, 2025, 9:00 PM, against a background near 1 ppb, over 3 hours.
Through the episode the wind came from the west-north-west, measured at the monitor.
The closest filed report is incident 434877 from Alon Usa Big Spring Refinery, listing 2233.6 pounds, with 100% of the episode's hours inside its window.

innocent_explanations: A release below the reportable quantity would leave no filed report at all.
Permitted, routine emissions can build up when the air is still and the plume stays low.
what_would_settle_it: Sub-hourly data from the monitor for this window, which would show whether the rise was a sharp plume or a slow build.
Any complaint or investigation records the agency holds for this date.
case.request_draft:
To: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality, Public Information Coordinator
Subject: Public information request, air monitoring and incident records, Big Spring

Dear Public Information Coordinator,

Under the Texas Public Information Act, I request copies of the following records.

1. All ambient air monitoring data, at the finest time resolution held, for monitor 48-227-1072 from Feb 25, 2025, 9:00 PM to Feb 26, 2025, 12:00 AM local time.
2. Any citizen complaints, investigation reports or field notes relating to air quality in Big Spring for that period.
3. Any emission event, maintenance, startup or shutdown notifications received for facilities in Howard County covering that period, including any submitted after the deadline.

This is a request for public records. It is not an allegation that any facility did anything improper.

If any portion is withheld, please cite the exemption claimed and release the remainder. If fees will exceed $50, please contact me first with an estimate.

Sincerely,
[your name]
[your address]
[your email and phone]
